definition: The rules both sides agree to when they sign a contract.
business_context_example: Please read the terms and conditions before you sign the training agreement.

definition: Breaking a promise or rule written in a contract.
business_context_example: Delivering three months late is a breach of contract, not a small delay.

definition: A separate section or rule inside a contract.
business_context_example: Clause 7 says either side can cancel with 30 days' notice.

definition: The part of a contract explaining how it can be ended.
business_context_example: The termination clause protects us if the client stops paying.

definition: The time you must give before ending a contract or leaving a job.
business_context_example: Her notice period is one month, so she leaves on 30 September.

definition: Legally forcing both sides to do what they agreed.
business_context_example: The email is friendly, but the signed order is what's binding.

definition: Having no legal effect at all.
business_context_example: Without a signature and a date, the annex is void.

definition: A written agreement to give up a right or claim.
business_context_example: They signed a waiver accepting the risk of the outdoor activity.

definition: To make an official change to a document.
business_context_example: We amended the contract to add a second training location.

definition: An unexpected event, like a flood or war, that excuses a party from performing.
business_context_example: The force majeure clause covered the closure during the lockdown.

definition: The country's law that will be used to interpret a contract.
business_context_example: The governing law is Bulgarian law, even though the client is German.

definition: Agreed in principle, but not legally binding until a contract is signed.
business_context_example: We accepted the price subject to contract, so nothing is final yet.

definition: Honestly and fairly, without trying to deceive.
business_context_example: Both sides negotiated in good faith and reached a compromise.

definition: Said in negotiation and not usable as evidence in court later.
business_context_example: The offer was made without prejudice, so it can't be quoted against us.
translation_bg: без да се засягат права (при преговори)

definition: Legal responsibility for damage, loss or debt.
business_context_example: Our liability is limited to the value of the contract.

definition: A promise to pay for another party's loss or damage.
business_context_example: The supplier gave an indemnity against any third-party claims.

definition: Failing to take reasonable care, causing harm to someone.
business_context_example: The court found negligence because no safety checks were done.

definition: Money paid to make up for loss or injury.
business_context_example: They claimed 40,000 euro in damages for the lost contract.

definition: To start a legal case against someone.
business_context_example: They threatened to sue, but the case never reached court.

definition: To end a dispute by agreement, without a trial.
business_context_example: It was cheaper to settle out of court than to fight for two years.

definition: The person or company bringing a legal case.
business_context_example: The claimant asked for both damages and legal costs.

definition: The person or company a legal case is brought against.
business_context_example: The defendant denied every point in the claim.

definition: A meeting in court where both sides present their arguments.
business_context_example: The hearing was postponed until November.

definition: A formal spoken statement given as evidence.
business_context_example: Her testimony about the delivery dates changed the case.

definition: The official decision at the end of a trial.
business_context_example: The verdict came after four days and went against the supplier.

definition: To ask a higher court to change a decision.
business_context_example: They lost, but they have 14 days to appeal.

definition: Settling a dispute with a private decision-maker instead of a court.
business_context_example: The contract sends any dispute to arbitration in Vienna.

definition: The process of taking a dispute through the courts.
business_context_example: Two years of litigation cost more than the original invoice.

definition: The time limit for bringing a legal claim.
business_context_example: The statute of limitations had passed, so the claim was rejected.

definition: To follow a rule, law or standard.
business_context_example: Every supplier must comply with our data protection policy.

definition: The act of following rules and laws that apply to your business.
business_context_example: Compliance training is mandatory for all new staff.

definition: An official rule made by a government or authority.
business_context_example: The new regulation changes how we store client records.

definition: Rules about collecting, storing and using personal information.
business_context_example: Data protection means we can't share student emails with partners.

definition: A contract promising to keep information secret.
business_context_example: Sign the non-disclosure agreement before we show you the figures.

definition: Meant to be kept secret from other people.
business_context_example: Salary information is confidential and stays with HR.

definition: Careful checking of facts before signing a deal.
business_context_example: Due diligence found two unpaid tax bills we hadn't seen.

definition: Legal rights over ideas, names, designs and creative work.
business_context_example: The course materials are our intellectual property, not the trainer's.

definition: A protected name, logo or sign that identifies a business.
business_context_example: We registered the trademark before launching in Greece.

definition: The right to control copying and use of creative work.
business_context_example: Copyright on the workbook stays with the school.

definition: A legal right stopping others from using an invention.
business_context_example: The patent runs out in 2031 and then anyone can copy it.

definition: Official permission to use something owned by someone else.
business_context_example: We bought a licence to use the software for 20 users.

definition: The document setting out how a company is run.
business_context_example: The articles of association say two directors must sign.

definition: A formal decision approved by a company's board.
business_context_example: We need a board resolution before opening the second office.

definition: A document letting one person act legally for another.
business_context_example: She signed under a power of attorney while the owner was abroad.

definition: A contract between company owners about how they work together.
business_context_example: The shareholder agreement explains what happens if one partner leaves.

definition: A company controlled by another company.
business_context_example: The Sofia office is a subsidiary of the German parent company.

definition: A lawyer who advises a person or company.
business_context_example: Legal counsel advised us not to reply until Monday.

definition: To write the first version of a contract.
business_context_example: Can you draft a contract for the 12-month corporate programme?

definition: To make sure a rule or contract is obeyed.
business_context_example: A clause you never enforce stops meaning very much.

definition: Legally responsible for something.
business_context_example: The tenant is liable for any damage beyond normal wear.
